newsitem.title: USA: N. Korea postpones missile talks with U.S.
newsitem.headline: N. Korea postpones missile talks with U.S.

text.p: North Korea has postponed talks with the United States set for next week on getting Pyongyang to halt its missile sales, the State Department said on Tuesday.
North Korea cited "technical reasons" for the delay but assured U.S. officials it wanted to reschedule the discussions for the near future, spokesman John Dinger said.
He refused to speculate on Pyongyang's reasoning for the delay but denied that U.S. efforts to forge improved ties with the Stalinist regime were in a downturn.
The missile talks had been set for May 12 and 13 in New York but "North Korea requested a postponement for what they described as technical reasons," Dinger told reporters.
However, "they assured us they look forward to the talks" and the United States expects to soon propose a new date a few weeks hence, perhaps around June 1, he said.
The United States has made clear its concern over Pyongyang's missile sales to Iran and Syria and said progress on this issue was critical to improved U.S.-North Korean ties.
At separate talks in New York two weeks ago, the United States and South Korea failed to get North Korea to join Korean peninsula peace negotiations.
"This is not an easy relationship but it is not all negative," Dinger said.
He noted that U.S. and North Korean officials this week resumed after a long hiatus discussions on American soldiers missing in action from the 1950-53 Korean War.

Also, North Korea is continuing to observe a 1994 landmark agreement with the United States under which Pyongyang agreed to freeze its nuclear programme in return for $4.5 billion in new nuclear power technology and alternative energy supplies.
Washington insists on progress in accounting for the MIAs and getting Pyongyang to halt missile sales as well as continued adherence to the nuclear accord as conditions for improved ties.
